<h2>SherlockEQ 0.3.3</h2>

<p>
  A maintenance release that polishes the Analog Control Unit. The OUTPUT row
  now lists only real speakers instead of macOS's internal audio plumbing, the
  menu-bar popover is easier to read, and there's a new in-app guide for the
  <code>sherlockeq</code> command-line tool added in 0.3.2.
</p>

<h3>Added</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>A Command-Line Tool help article.</strong>
    The in-app Help (and the website) now has a full guide to
    <code>sherlockeq</code> — how to install it, every command at a glance, and
    a few ready-to-use scripting workflows.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Changed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>The menu-bar popover is easier to read.</strong>
    The output-device label and the Quit button are larger and clearer.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Debug is now opt-in.</strong>
    The Debug screen is hidden from the main window's sidebar by default; turn
    it on under Settings → Diagnostics if you want it. When enabled, it now
    shows a live dynamics readout, per-stage signal-chain bypass switches, and a
    tidier layout.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Fixed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>The OUTPUT row only shows real speakers now.</strong>
    macOS quietly creates temporary internal devices to route the default
    output; these were leaking into the panel as a stray button with a question
    mark. They're now filtered out, so you only see devices you can actually
    pick. Any device that isn't recognised shows a generic speaker icon instead
    of a question mark, and the row is capped at six buttons so it can't overrun
    the panel.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>The spectrum analyzer panel opens and closes cleanly.</strong>
    Toggling it quickly could leave the window and the arrow out of sync — the
    panel showing while the window stayed short, or vice versa. It now stays in
    step no matter how fast you click.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Tables render properly in Help.</strong>
    Markdown tables (including the ones on the Keyboard Shortcuts page) were
    showing as raw <code>| a | b |</code> text; they're now laid out as real
    tables.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Not a medical device</h3>

<p>
  SherlockEQ is not a healthcare or medical application. It does not diagnose,
  treat, measure, or monitor any hearing condition, tinnitus, or disability.
  For concerns about your hearing, consult a doctor, audiologist, or licensed
  healthcare professional.
</p>
